Implementation Plan

Plan for issue #6232: run the unblock judge's Claude path in the isolated container

Planning ref: `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7` @ `dd96ae9fc8592ce8b4a12207f126099602c6caf5` (matches the integration branch metadata; no mismatch).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh
Scope-mode justification: The finding is real. `scripts/unblock_judge.sh:672-675` calls the host-side `claude_run UNBLOCK_JUDGE ... "${TARGET_DIR}"`, so Claude Code runs on the runner. The relay's OAuth token, `RUNNER_TEMP` (where the Claude pool tokens live) and the rest of the filesystem are all readable from there. Meanwhile the model reads untrusted comments, PR diffs and run logs. Unsetting `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`TG_BOT_SECRET`/`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` does not protect the Claude credential. The repo already has the fix pattern. `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` has a Claude branch that runs `claude -p` with `--network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL`, only `Read,Grep,Glob`, and a placeholder `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; the real token stays in `scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py` on the host. That branch is limited to `CLARIFY|CLARIFY_RESPOND` (line 14). The full fix has two parts: allow `UNBLOCK_JUDGE` on that branch, and have the judge call the runner with `claude` instead of `claude_run`. That is a few lines per file, adds no new dependency and no new interface. Per §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the complete fix wins. The judge passes a 1500 s timeout that the Claude branch currently ignores; honouring it there costs about 6 lines, so it is included. Other host-side `claude_run` callers (`scripts/run_plan_codex.sh:291`, PLAN) are a related surface but outside this finding; they are listed under risks, not changed.

## §20.E automation surface
- New script: none. The change extends `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` and modifies `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`.
- Scheduler / entry point: unchanged. `.github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml`, step "Judge the blocked item", is dispatched by `unblock_judge_dispatch.yml` from the poller's unblock scan (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, `*/5` via `internal-orchestrate-poll.yml`). Nothing new to wire.
- Long-running supervisor: none needed.
- DB work: none.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`: no entry, because no new script is added.

## 1. Files likely to change
1. `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`: the model-invocation block in the judge function (around lines 666-685).
2. `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh`: the Claude role guard (line 14) and the in-container command of the Claude branch.
3. `tests/test_unblock_judge.py`: new contract and behaviour tests.
4. `tests/test_plan_clarify_header_prompt_staging.py`: update the runner role and timeout assertions.
5. `.github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml`: comment-only update above "Install Claude Code CLI" (lines 125-127), which still says `claude_run` falls back to codex. Step names, ids and env stay the same.
6. `agents.md`: the "Unblock judge (Phase 7)" paragraph (line 1779) and the clarify isolation sentence in "Workflow architecture" item 2 (both engines now isolated for UNBLOCK_JUDGE).
7. `README.md`: the `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_MODEL` row (line 90).
8. `changelog.d/6232-unblock-judge-claude-isolation.md`: new fragment (CLAUDE.md §20; `<!-- changelog: security -->` or `fixed`, following existing fragments such as `changelog.d/summariser-inline-inputs-only.md`).

## 2. Functions and modules to change

`scripts/unblock_judge.sh`, judge-run block (the `if [ "${engine}" = "claude" ]` branch):
- Remove the subshell `( unset ...; claude_run UNBLOCK_JUDGE "${prompt_file}" "${output_file}" "${TARGET_DIR}" )`.
- Replace it with a call to the isolated runner that mirrors the existing codex call:
  ```
  (cd "${TARGET_DIR}" && env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u TG_BOT_SECRET -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY \
      MODEL_EDITOR="${model}" MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT="${reasoning}" \
      CLARIFY_ISOLATION_SUPPORT_DIR="${SUPPORT_DIR}/scripts" \
      CLARIFY_ISOLATION_TIMEOUT_SECS="${UNBLOCK_JUDGE_TIMEOUT_SECS:-1500}" \
      bash "${SUPPORT_DIR}/scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh" "${prompt_file}" "${output_file}" "${RUNTIME_DIR}/claude.err" claude UNBLOCK_JUDGE) || rc=$?
  ```
- Keep the existing return-code contract:
  - rc 0: use the output.
  - rc 75: the Claude engine is unavailable (no credential, image build failed, all accounts failed). Fall through to the existing isolated codex call, as today.
  - Any other rc: log `UNBLOCK_JUDGE item=... kind=... stop=... outcome=model_failed reason=isolation_failed rc=<n>` (same log key and reason as the codex path) and truncate `output_file`. Do not run codex; this matches today's behaviour, where a non-75 host Claude failure never ran codex.
- Leave `source ai_engine.sh` and `ai_engine_for_role` engine selection unchanged. After this change `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` contains no `claude_run` reference.
- Add a code comment: the Claude credential stays in the host relay; the model never runs on the host.

`scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh`:
- Line 14: widen the Claude role guard to `^(CLARIFY|CLARIFY_RESPOND|UNBLOCK_JUDGE)$`. Line 13 already accepts UNBLOCK_JUDGE, and `.github/ai/claude_engine.json` gives `UNBLOCK_JUDGE` profile `read`. The branch already hard-codes `--profile read` and `--tools Read,Grep,Glob`.
- Claude branch `docker run`:
  - Add `--env "CLARIFY_ISOLATION_TIMEOUT_SECS=${isolation_timeout}"`.
  - In the container script, wrap the `claude -p ...` command in `timeout "${CLARIFY_ISOLATION_TIMEOUT_SECS}"` when it is set, using the same if/else shape as the codex branch. If it is empty the command runs as today, so `clarify.yml` and `orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml`, which do not set it, behave the same.
  - A timeout makes rc 124. `_ai_engine_py classify` then gives `timeout` or `crashed`, the `*)` arm exits 1, and the judge logs `isolation_failed`.

## 3. Data structures affected
None. Verdict JSON, ledger markers (`<!-- ai:unblock:v1 ... -->`), the run directory layout (new `${RUNTIME_DIR}/claude.err` log file only) and the state comments are unchanged.

## 4. API and interface changes
- `clarify_isolated_run.sh <prompt> <out> <log> claude UNBLOCK_JUDGE` is newly accepted. Previously it exited 1 with `Invalid Claude engine role`.
- The Claude branch now honours `CLARIFY_ISOLATION_TIMEOUT_SECS`. This is an existing env var, optional, with no default, so callers that don't set it see no change (§8 satisfied).
- No new env vars, workflow inputs or log prefixes. `CLAUDE_POOL`, `AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK` and `UNBLOCK_JUDGE` lines keep their shape; `CLAUDE_POOL ... role=UNBLOCK_JUDGE` now appears from the runner.
- No new GitHub API calls (§14).

Data flow:
1. `unblock_judge.sh` builds `prompt.txt` (untrusted context) in `RUNTIME_DIR`.
2. `ai_engine_for_role UNBLOCK_JUDGE` picks the engine.
3. If it picks claude, `clarify_isolated_run.sh ... claude UNBLOCK_JUDGE` (cwd = `TARGET_DIR`):
   - snapshots only tracked safe files to `/source`;
   - the host relay holds the token from `$(ai_engine_pool_dir)/tokens/<account>`;
   - the container (no network, read-only, placeholder token) runs `claude -p`;
   - the transcript is classified and extracted to `output_file`.
4. On rc 75, the existing isolated codex path runs. On any other non-zero rc, the judge logs `model_failed` and the output stays empty, which leads to an `invalid_verdict` wait comment.
5. Verdict parse, secret rejection and actuation run unchanged.

Failure modes:
- Docker image build fails on the Claude branch. Symptom: `AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK role=UNBLOCK_JUDGE reason=image_build_failed`. Recovery: rc 75, isolated codex runs.
- No pool credential. Symptom: `AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK reason=no_credential`. Recovery: rc 75, isolated codex runs.
- Relay crashes, or every account is rate-limited or fails auth. Symptom: `CLAUDE_POOL ... outcome=crashed|usage_limit|auth_failed`, then `all_accounts_failed`. Recovery: rc 75, codex runs.
- Claude times out or crashes in the container. Symptom: `UNBLOCK_JUDGE ... outcome=model_failed reason=isolation_failed rc=1`. Recovery: `invalid_verdict` wait comment; the next scan retries after `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_RETRY_HOURS`.
- Source snapshot rejected (unsafe tracked path). Symptom: runner exits 1, then `isolation_failed`. Recovery: same as the timeout case. This is fail-closed and never falls back to host Claude.

## Decisions

### D1 — Reuse the clarify isolated runner's Claude branch
- Chosen: route UNBLOCK_JUDGE's Claude engine through `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` (`claude UNBLOCK_JUDGE`), widening its Claude role allow-list.
- Alternatives considered: (a) a new unblock-specific container runner; (b) hardening `claude_run` on the host (sandboxing the Read tool or deny-listing paths); (c) forcing UNBLOCK_JUDGE to codex only.
- Why: (a) duplicates a reviewed isolation boundary (§9: extend, don't compete). (b) still leaves the token on the same host the model reads from, which is what the finding flags. (c) drops a supported engine and breaks the `AI_ENGINE_UNBLOCK_JUDGE` / `ai:engine-claude` selection. The runner already keeps the OAuth token in a host relay and gives the container only a placeholder, which is exactly what the recommendation asks for.

### D2 — Keep the rc 75 to codex fallback, and keep "no codex" on other Claude failures
- Chosen: preserve today's return-code semantics.
- Alternatives considered: fall back to codex on every Claude failure.
- Why: §2 rule 1 (preserve existing behaviour). An rc 1 can come from a fail-closed security check such as a snapshot rejection; retrying on another engine would hide it.

### D3 — Honour the isolation timeout on the Claude branch
- Chosen: wrap `claude -p` in `timeout` only when `CLARIFY_ISOLATION_TIMEOUT_SECS` is set.
- Alternatives considered: leave the Claude branch without a timeout.
